problem: The compensation direction is wrong. V_T rises with temperature, so g_m = I_C/V_T falls and r_e = V_T/I_E rises at fixed bias. Lowering the bias current makes g_m fall further and r_e rise further; it does not compensate.
fix: Treating 26 mV as a constant. V_T = kT/q rises with temperature, so g_m falls and r_e rises unless the bias current is raised in proportion to V_T (a PTAT bias). With I_C ∝ V_T, g_m = I_C/V_T and r_e = V_T/I_E stay fixed.

problem: A_v = −g_m(R_L ∥ r_o) is the gain of a loaded stage, not the intrinsic gain. In standard usage the intrinsic gain is g_m r_o, the gain with the output open. Calling the loaded value 'intrinsic' can confuse a student who meets the term g_m r_o later.
fix: Ask for the stage voltage gain with R_L and r_o included: A_v = −g_m(R_L ∥ r_o). Reserve 'intrinsic gain' for g_m r_o.

problem: V_T = kT/q is written without saying what k and q are, though every other symbol is defined.
fix: V_T = kT/q where k is the Boltzmann constant (1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K), T is the absolute temperature in kelvin and q is the electron charge (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C); at T ≈ 300 K, V_T ≈ 26 mV.
